Alex: Heads up — after the runtime patch that changed CUDA graph capture ordering, we've seen a 15-25% p95 latency regression on multi-GPU TP workloads. Repro on dedicated-xyz cluster.
Priya: Which patch? kernel selection or batching heuristics?
Alex: The change was in graph capture: we started capturing kernels on an external stream to reduce main-stream stalls. It used to be: capture on compute stream, now: capture -> schedule copy to external stream -> replay.
Jorge: Hmm. That can affect comm/compute overlap if all-reduce expects ops on the compute stream. Any traces?
Alex: Yep, attached a condensed perf trace. Key snippet:
```
Timeline:
  stream 0 (compute): kernel A -> kernel B -> waitEvent(e1)
  stream 3 (external): cudaGraphLaunch -> allreduce_kickoff -> allreduce
  sync: event e1 recorded on stream 3 then waited on stream 0
Result: allreduce runs, but compute stream is blocked on the event — no overlap.
```
Mei: So the capture moved the event ordering such that the compute stream waits for the external stream's event instead of overlapping. That would serialize comm and compute.
Priya: What about KV cache prefetch paths? Are they touching the same external stream? Could be another source of ordering.
Alex: Good catch — KV prefetch uses stream 3 for async copies in this config. We now have two users of stream 3: graph replay and kv-prefetch copies. Race observed.
Jorge: Profiling numbers?
Alex: Baseline (before patch): p95 = 312ms, allreduce overlap avg = 42% of allreduce time overlapped with compute. After patch: p95 = 387ms, overlap = 4-8% on 8xTP runs.
Mei: Oof. Any stack logs from NCCL? Could be fallback to blocking collectives if streams aren't correctly marked.
Alex: NCCL logs show normal allreduce launch but timeline shows it executes on the external stream while compute waits on event recorded later.
Priya: Hypothesis: cudaGraphCapture on external stream is inserting event-records that are not seen as stream-compatible with pre-existing encode of collectives, causing waitEvent semantics. Alternatively, graph replay may be using implicit stream synchronization when launched from a different stream context.
Mei: Also check driver behavior with cudaLaunchGraph — there are subtle semantics when captured kernels synchronize with host or other streams.
Jorge: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) Replay the graph on the original compute stream (undo the capture redirection). 2) Use streamWaitEvent ordering carefully: ensure events are recorded on compute stream and waited on external stream, not the other way around. 3) Isolate KV prefetch to a dedicated stream per replica to avoid cross-use.
Alex: I tried forcing replay on compute stream — overlap returns and p95 goes back within 5% of baseline. But that undoes the original optimization for capture latency.
Priya: We need a long-term fix in kernel selection / capture path: when compiling a graph, mark which streams hold comm kernels and ensure replay semantics preserve original stream ordering. Also update batching heuristics so KV prefetch doesn't default to the graph's external stream.
Mei: Can we add a test that asserts comm/compute overlap isn't reduced across capture/replay permutations? Add to perf regression harness with synthetic TP+KV workload.
Alex: Added a failing test in my branch (link: github.com/redwood/runtime/PR/xxxx). It reproduces on nightly gpu-4 nodes.
infra-bot: Deploy alert: dedicated-xyz was auto-rolled back to previous runtime build at 00:22 UTC due to SLO breaches.
Jorge: Good. For next steps: (a) revert capture redirection for the short term, (b) change KV prefetch default stream allocation, (c) add unit/integration perf test, (d) add telemetry to detect when compute stream is waiting on external-stream events.
Priya: Also verify NCCL version interaction — some versions changed behavior when collectives are launched from graphs. Add a matrix run.
Mei: I'll take (c) + telemetry. Jorge you want to own (a) revert? Alex can drive (b) KV prefetch isolation and the PR with the failing test.
Jorge: I'll cut the revert PR now and coordinate with infra to re-deploy a rollback-safe change.
Alex: Will post a short repro script and nvprof capture. Repro uses 8x TP, seq_len 1024, batch 16, kv-prefetch enabled.
Priya: Thanks — keep the channel updated. If anyone sees related incidents in other clusters, ping here. :pray:
Mei: Also logging note: instrument event-record/ wait pairs and include stream ids in perf dumps. That will make future triage much faster.
Alex: Agreed. Uploading traces and a minimal repro to the PR.
Jorge: Thanks team. We'll aim to get a safe revert and follow-ups in today's sprint. :thumbsup:
